doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Musical family and a father who left music for mathematics
summary: Ann says everyone in her family plays; her father, raised on the Lower East Side, became a mathematician but always played, and her brother got the lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. That is an important thing. We’ll talk about that. But I’m curious, where do these music genes come from in your family?

I don’t know. I’m not a biologist. But everybody in the family plays. My father, I guess his family thought of musicians as being basically one up from beggars. He was raised on the Lower East Side and had known these Klezmer musicians. And it was not looked on as any important thing. And so although he played music, he went to Cornell and he got a degree. And he was going to write the great novel, you know, be a writer, but then he discovered mathematics and he became a mathematician. But he always played music. And when I was coming up I thought all grownups played music. I assumed that I would be playing music. And actually my brother was the one that got the lessons. I was not. But I’d always wanted to play. And so as an adult, or as an older kid I did.
